newsitem.title: USA: Minnesota school funding case to proceed.
newsitem.headline: Minnesota school funding case to proceed.

text.p: A lawsuit seeking more state funding for Minneapolis public schools will proceed to trial after the Minnesota Supreme Court declined to take up aspects of the case, according to an attorney working on the case.

Jeane-Marie Almonor, an attorney representing the plaintiffs in the case, the local branch of the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People and the parents of school children enrolled in the city schools, said Wednesday the state's high court declined to give the trial court guidance in the case.
A Hennepin County District Court judge had forwarded certain questions pertaining to the case to the high court in a request for guidance.
"The supreme court said it was premature and that the case should proceed to trial," Almonor said.

Almonor said parties to the case were expected to meet with the trial court judge next month to set up a schedule for trial. In the meantime, she said the plaintiffs and the state were also exploring mediation as ordered by the trial court.

The NAACP filed the class-action lawsuit in 1995. The lawsuit charged that students in Minneapolis were deprived of an adequate education because their schools are segregated and that the edcuation offered in those schools is unequal to education provided in suburban Minneapolis school districts.
The lawsuit seeks injuntive relief in the way the school district is set up and operated in addition to more state funding.
